newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- A peace accord at Anglo American Platinum Mines is in tatters afer the murder of two more National Union of Mineworkers officials and four of their relatives at Amplats and in the Eastern Cape.

- Senior staff at the Development Bank of Southern Africa have approached Finance Minister Trevor Manuel to express dissatisfaction over the appointment of foreigners and the bank's affirmative action policies, sources said.
- The Financial Services Board said it would intensify its investigations into unregistered, and therefore illegal, long-term life assurers operating in South Africa.

- The African National Congress national executive committee has endorsed peace talks with the Inkatha Freedom Party, but expressed reservations about a special amnesty for KwaZulu-Natal, ANC sources said.

- The Office for Serious Economic Offences was investigating cases involving about 12 billion rand -- "a drop in the ocean" compared with commercial crime cases reported to the police, director Jan Swanepoel said.
- South African Forestry Company management and labour have reached agreement on the parastatal's restructuring, including that it should not be split up, but they are deadlocked on several issues.
- Swaziland's cabinet has approved construction of Eskom's 400kV power line through Swaziland to feed Gencor's Mozal aluminium smelter plant in Mozambique.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The National Union of Mineworkers would lose millions of rand in subscriptions if 100,000 mineworkers facing retrenchment were axed, NUM President James Motlatsi said.
- The South African Black Taxi Association plans to set up a nationwide chain of cooperatives as part of a commercialisation drive, an official said.
- Sasol Gas, the gas supply division of synthetic fuel producer Sasol, said it had signed a multimillion rand deal to supply methane-rich gas to power the Alusaf Hillside smelter in Richards Bay.
- Sourcecon Technology Solutions (STS), a black controlled information technology group, has won a hard-fought contract to supply Compaq computer hardware to Telkom over the next year.

- Soap operas are becoming big business in more ways than one. Egoli, South Africa's home-grown soap opera, has been flooded with endorsements from companies looking for a cost- effective alternative to high-cost prime-time TV advertising.
SAKE-BEELD
- South African economists are currently more optimistic about the prospects for the rand than they were at the beginning of the year.
- The South African Mint has won a tender to strike new coins for New Zealand.
- Kairinos Foods said it had decided to withdraw its current prospectus and postpone its proposed listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, planned for later this month.
- A final decision on the Coega harbour project in the Eastern Cape is likely this week and the signs are good that the government will approve the plan.
THE STAR

- A two billion rand, three-year plan to make Johannesburg the premier economic and tourist centre of South Africa could see the city centre linked directly to Pretoria and the airport by a high-speed rail network.
- A flight from Cape Town to Johannesburg at the weekend had to make an emergency landing when the wing-flaps refused to operate.
